comparison: Perfect agreement on intergenic NMIs and lncRNA associations (C46-C49). Both evaluations accept the findings, though peer reviewers' general request for orthogonal validation (Comment 1) applies to all NMIs including these.

Strong agreement on the three-class NMI classification system and conservation conclusions (C69-C77). Both accept the conceptual framework and synthesis. OpenEval notes some speculation about selective pressure; peer reviewers focus on methodological validation rather than challenging the interpretive framework.

Agreement on broad NMIs and their association with developmental genes and polycomb marks (C60-C66, C74). Both evaluations accept the GO analysis, ChIP-seq data, and Hox cluster examples without challenge.

Disagreement on TSS-NMI associations (C36-C43). OpenEval finds strong quantitative support from Figure 2A data. Peer reviewers question the framing as 'contrary to expectations' (Comment 4) and request orthogonal validation of NMIs (Comment 1), indicating uncertainty about methodology despite not challenging the data directly.

Agreement on tissue-specific NMIs and their properties (C52-C59, C78). Both accept the differential methylation findings, H3K4me3 correlations, and statistical associations with gene expression. Peer reviewers did not challenge these plastic NMI characterizations.

Agreement on NMI conservation at orthologous genes (C44-C45). Both evaluations accept the hypergeometric test results and highly significant p-values demonstrating evolutionary conservation across species comparisons.

Agreement on nucleotide composition analysis (C18-C28). Both accept the species-specific variations in CpG O/E and GC content. Peer reviewers acknowledge prior description of this variability (Comment 3) and request citation and clearer explanation, but do not challenge the findings.

Disagreement on CGI prediction failure and Bio-CAP methodology (C16, C31-C34). OpenEval finds comprehensive evidence for discordance and methodological superiority. Peer reviewers accept work as 'well executed' but explicitly request orthogonal validation of NMIs (Comment 1) and acknowledgment of potential species-specific performance differences (Comments 2, 5), indicating uncertainty about the methodology.

Agreement on need to re-evaluate CGI-based predictions (C35). Both accept that experimental NMI data reveals limitations of sequence-based approaches. Peer reviewers' acceptance for publication indicates agreement with this strong conclusion.

Agreement on evolutionary mechanisms explaining sequence variation (C29-C30). OpenEval cites literature support and mechanistic explanation. Peer reviewers accept these findings and request appropriate citation (Comment 3) and clearer summary (Comment 2), indicating agreement.

Agreement on H3K4me3 enrichment at NMIs (C58-C59). Both evaluations accept the ChIP-seq data showing tissue-specific histone modification patterns corresponding to NMI presence across multiple species.

Partial overlap on Bio-CAP methodology and TSS associations (C4, C17). OpenEval supports TSS-NMI findings; peer reviewers request orthogonal validation and acknowledgment of potential CpG-density biases in affinity-based assays, indicating methodological uncertainty.

Peer reviewers address framing of expectations about NMIs at promoters (C15, C68), noting that NMIs at promoters should not be surprising (Comment 4). No corresponding OpenEval result specifically addresses the expectation framing, though R2 discusses the TSS association data itself.
